intro: The Pediatric Drug Formulary screen gives clinicians searchable access to dosage information drawn from two named references — Neofax for neonatology and the Harriet Lane Handbook for general paediatrics — plus dedicated Emergency NICU and Emergency PICU drug sections. Users pick a source, then search or browse entries that link to a page reference in the original formulary text. On iOS, the app displays an educational-use disclaimer banner reminding users to verify against current clinical guidelines and institutional protocols.
indications: Looking up neonatal drug dosing (Neofax-sourced) during NICU care
Looking up general paediatric drug dosing (Harriet Lane Handbook-sourced)
Rapid access to emergency NICU drugs (infusions, resuscitation medications) during a crisis
Rapid access to emergency PICU STAT bolus and infusion drugs during a crisis
Cross-checking a drug's page reference in the source formulary text
method: This is a reference/search tool rather than a calculator: it has no formula. It lets the user choose a source — Neofax (labelled 'Neonatology,' 200 drugs) or the Harriet Lane Handbook (labelled 'Paediatrics,' 457 drugs) — then search or browse an alphabetical list of drug entries, each linking to a page reference in a PDF viewer. Separate shortcut cards open Emergency NICU Drugs (14 drugs, described as infusions/resuscitation) and Emergency PICU Drugs (10 STAT bolus drugs plus 9 infusions).

faqs.q: What sources does the drug formulary draw from?
faqs.a: The app states its dosage information comes from Neofax and the Harriet Lane Handbook.

faqs.q: How many drugs are in the formulary?
faqs.a: The app's feature description cites 676 drugs total on the full web app, split in-app into 200 Neofax (Neonatology) entries and 457 Harriet Lane (Paediatrics) entries.

faqs.q: Is there a fast path to emergency drug dosing?
faqs.a: Yes — dedicated Emergency NICU Drugs (14 drugs) and Emergency PICU Drugs (10 STAT bolus + 9 infusions) shortcut cards sit above the main source selector.

faqs.q: Does the app warn against relying on it as the sole source?
faqs.a: On iOS, an educational disclaimer banner tells users the content is "for educational and reference use only" and to verify against current clinical guidelines and institutional protocols.

faqs.q: How is a specific drug entry displayed?
faqs.a: Search results show the drug name and its page number in the source formulary, opening into a PDF viewer screen.
